title: Interpreting events in a sequence
blurb: Put events in the order they actually happened, even when a passage tells them out of order, using signal words, dates and verb tense.
question: A passage begins, 'By the time the ambulance reached the hospital, Dr. Reyes had already scrubbed in,' and then describes the 911 call made twenty minutes earlier. A question asks which event happened first. Why is the ambulance's arrival the wrong answer even though it is mentioned first?

teach.h: Order of occurrence, not order of mention
teach.body: Formally, interpreting a sequence means identifying the chronological or logical order of events or steps: what happened first, next, last, before or after a given event, and what step is missing. In plain English: rebuild the real timeline. Writers often start in the middle or at the end and then look back, but TEAS questions always ask about the order in which things actually happened.

teach.h: Signal words and what they tell you
head: Signal
Examples
Tells you
rows: before, previously, by the time, until
teach.caption: Also: finally, eventually, at last, later, as soon as, plus any dates and clock times.

teach.h: Model passage: told out of order
teach.body:
(1) By the time the ambulance reached Mercy Hospital, Dr. Reyes had already scrubbed in. (2) Twenty minutes earlier, a dispatcher had taken a 911 call from a construction site. (3) While paramedics were loading the injured worker into the ambulance, the charge nurse phoned the operating room. (4) That call led the team to postpone a routine knee surgery and prepare for the new patient.

Sentence 1 is mentioned first but happens last.

items.label: Paramedics load worker; nurse calls OR

teach.caption: The loading and the phone call share one slot: 'while' makes them simultaneous.

teach.body: The past perfect ('had scrubbed in', 'had taken') marks an action completed before another past action. 'By the time A happened, B had happened' means B came first. 'Before this, ...' and 'twenty minutes earlier' send you backward. 'Meanwhile', 'while' and 'during' do the opposite of sequencing: they place two events side by side in time, so neither is 'before' the other.

items: Underline every date, time and signal word in the passage.
Circle past perfect verbs (had + verb): those events come earlier.
Sketch a quick timeline on scratch paper and place each event on it.
Put simultaneous events in the same slot.
Reread the stem: first, last, immediately before or immediately after? Answer that exact relation.

teach.h: A process sequence: filling a prescription
teach.caption: Process passages use logical order. A step from a different process (like 'patient schedules a follow-up') does not belong in the chain.

teach.text: Sequence traps: choosing the order of mention instead of the order of occurrence; reversing 'before' and 'after' (read the stem twice); treating simultaneous events as one after the other; and accepting an option that slips in a step from a different process or one the passage never mentions.

teach.body: Kevin Nguyen, applying to a paramedic-to-RN bridge program, must drag four events into order. The passage opens with a graduation, then says 'It had all started three years earlier.' Kevin sketches a timeline: the start three years back goes first, the graduation last. He spots 'meanwhile' joining two events and keeps them in the same step of his sketch, then orders the rest by their dates.

items: TEAS sequence items ask for the order events happened, not the order they are told.
Signal words: first, then, after, before, previously, by the time, meanwhile, finally.
Past perfect (had + verb) marks an earlier event.
While, meanwhile and during mark simultaneous events.
Answer the exact relation in the stem: first, last, immediately before or immediately after.

summary: You can now rebuild the true order of events in narrative and process passages, using signal words, dates and past perfect verbs. You can also avoid the order-of-mention, before/after and simultaneous-event traps.

A.q:
Read the passage.

Mia finally passed her nursing assistant certification exam in May. She had failed the skills portion in January, after practicing the skills only from online videos. In February, she joined a study group that met in the community college lab. By April, she could complete every skill within the time limit.

Which event happened immediately after Mia failed the skills portion?
options: She passed her certification exam
She joined a study group at the lab
She practiced the skills from videos
She finished every skill on time
A.why: She failed in January and joined the study group in February, the next event on the timeline.

whyNot.0: She passed in May, the last event, not the one right after January.
whyNot.2: Practicing from videos came before the January failure ('after practicing...').
whyNot.3: She could finish every skill on time by April, after joining the study group.

A.q: In the sentence 'Meanwhile, the night nurse reviewed the morning lab results,' the word 'meanwhile' tells the reader that the review happened:
options: during the event just described
after the event just described had ended
before the event just described had begun
in place of the event just described
A.why: 'Meanwhile' signals simultaneous action: during the same period as the event just described.

whyNot.1: 'Afterward' or 'then' would signal a later event; 'meanwhile' does not.
whyNot.2: 'Previously' or 'before this' would signal an earlier event, not an overlapping one.
whyNot.3: 'Instead' signals a replacement, not a time relationship.

A.q:
Read the passage.

When you arrive at the blood drive, a staff member checks your ID and gives you an information sheet to read. Next comes a brief health screening, in which your temperature, blood pressure and iron level are checked. The donation itself takes about 10 minutes. Afterward, you rest and have a snack for 15 minutes before leaving.

According to the passage, what happens immediately before the donation?
options: Reading the information sheet
Having your ID checked by staff
Resting and having a snack
The brief health screening
A.why: The order is ID check and information sheet, then the health screening ('Next comes'), then the donation. The screening comes immediately before it.

whyNot.0: Reading the sheet happens on arrival, before the screening.
whyNot.1: The ID check is the first step, two steps before the donation.

B.q:
Read the passage.

The new wing of Cedar Hospital opened to patients in 2024. Construction had started in 2021, two years after the hospital board approved the plan. Before the board voted, a community survey found that most residents wanted more maternity beds.

Which list shows the events in the order they occurred?
options: Wing opens, construction starts, board approves, survey
Board approves, survey, construction starts, wing opens
Survey, board approves, construction starts, wing opens
Survey, construction starts, board approves, wing opens
B.why: The survey came before the vote; the board approved in 2019 (two years before 2021); construction started in 2021; the wing opened in 2024.

whyNot.0: This follows the order of mention, roughly reversed from the order of occurrence.
whyNot.1: The survey came before the board voted, not after.
whyNot.3: Construction started two years after the board approved the plan, so the approval comes first.

B.q:
Read the passage.

While the dental hygienist cleaned Mr. Ford's teeth, the dentist reviewed his X-rays in the next room. After the cleaning, the dentist examined Mr. Ford and found a small cavity. The receptionist then scheduled a filling for the following week.

Which two events happened at the same time?
options: The X-ray review and the dentist's exam
The cleaning and the dentist's exam
The exam and scheduling the filling
The cleaning and the X-ray review
B.why: 'While' links the cleaning and the X-ray review: they happened at the same time.

whyNot.0: The exam came 'after the cleaning', so it followed the X-ray review.
whyNot.1: The exam happened after the cleaning was finished.
whyNot.2: The receptionist scheduled the filling 'then', after the exam.

B.q:
Read the passage.

When Leah arrived at the pharmacy at 5:00 p.m., she learned that her prescription had been ready since noon. The pharmacist had called her at 12:15, but Leah had left her phone at home. She paid for the medicine and drove home.

Which of these events happened first?
options: The prescription was ready
The pharmacist called Leah
Leah arrived at the pharmacy
Leah paid for the medicine
B.why: The prescription was ready at noon, the earliest time given. The call came at 12:15, and Leah arrived at 5:00 p.m.

whyNot.1: The call was at 12:15, after the prescription was ready at noon.
whyNot.2: Leah arrived at 5:00 p.m., even though her arrival is mentioned first.
whyNot.3: She paid after arriving at 5:00 p.m.

C.q:
Read the passage.

Carlos stood at the podium to accept his nursing pin, thinking back to the day he almost quit. It was during his first semester, right after he failed his first pharmacology exam. That night, his grandmother sat with him and urged him not to give up. He hired a tutor the next morning, and by the end of that year he was tutoring other students himself.

Which event occurred third?
options: Carlos's grandmother spoke with him
Carlos began tutoring other students
Carlos accepted his nursing pin
Carlos hired a tutor
C.why: The order is: failed the exam; that night, his grandmother spoke with him; the next morning, he hired a tutor (third); by year's end, he tutored others; years later, he accepted his pin.

whyNot.0: The talk with his grandmother came 'that night', second in the sequence.
whyNot.1: Tutoring others came by the end of the year, fourth.
whyNot.2: The pinning is mentioned first but happened last.

C.q:
Read the passage.

The Brookfield town council voted in June to build a skate park. In the months before the vote, students had collected 900 signatures, and a local architect had donated a design. After the vote, the parks department chose a site, and construction began the following spring.

Which event happened BEFORE the council voted?
options: The parks department chose a site
A local architect donated a design
The council approved the skate park
Construction of the park began
C.why: 'In the months before the vote' places the donated design (and the signatures) earlier than the June vote.

whyNot.0: The site was chosen 'after the vote'.
whyNot.2: The approval is the vote itself, so it cannot come before the vote.
whyNot.3: Construction began the following spring, well after the vote.

C.q:
Read the procedure.

Before entering any data, the technician logs in to the analyzer. The quality-control check runs as soon as the technician logs in. Each sample tube is scanned after the quality-control check is passed but before the tube is loaded into the rack. Results print once the loaded sample finishes processing.

Which list gives the steps in the correct order?
options: Log in, run QC check, scan tube, load rack, print results
Log in, scan tube, run QC check, load rack, print results
Run QC check, log in, scan tube, load rack, print results
Log in, run QC check, load rack, scan tube, print results
C.why: Log in first; the QC check runs as soon as you log in; scanning comes after QC but before loading; results print after processing.

whyNot.1: Scanning comes after the QC check is passed, not before it.
whyNot.2: The QC check runs as soon as the technician logs in, so logging in comes first.
whyNot.3: The tube is scanned before it is loaded into the rack.

reteach.title: Your social media feed runs backward
reteach.question: A friend posts photos from a five-day trip, and your feed shows the newest post at the top. How do you work out what happened on day 1?

blocks.h: Display order is not event order
blocks.body: The feed shows the trip in reverse: the flight home first, the arrival last. Nobody thinks the trip started with the flight home; you scroll down to find the beginning. A passage that opens with an ending ('By the time the ambulance arrived...') is the same. The order things appear on the page is display order. The TEAS asks for the order they happened.

blocks.text: The first thing you see is not the first thing that happened. Rebuild the timeline before you answer.

explain.body: Sequence words place events in time: first, then, after, before, previously, by the time, finally. Same-time words: while, meanwhile, during, simultaneously.

test.q:
Read the passage.

Initially, the clinic used paper sign-in sheets. Eventually, it switched to a tablet check-in. In between, it tried a numbered-ticket system for one year.

Which system did the clinic use second?
options: Paper sign-in sheets
Numbered tickets
Tablet check-in
Phone check-in
test.why: 'Initially' paper, 'in between' tickets, 'eventually' tablets. The tickets came second.

whyNot.0: 'Initially' marks paper sheets as the first system.
whyNot.2: 'Eventually' marks the tablet as the last system.

explain.body: Passages may open with a later event and look back. Past perfect (had + verb) and phrases like 'earlier' or 'by the time' mark the earlier events.

explain.h: 'By the time she arrived, the bus had left'

test.q:
Read the sentence.

'By the time Ray finished his shift, his daughter had already fallen asleep, so he read the note she had left on the table.'

Which event happened first?
options: Ray finished his shift
Ray read his daughter's note
Ray's daughter left a note
Ray got home from work
test.why: 'Had left' is past perfect: the note was left before Ray finished his shift and before he read it. Of the events listed, it is the earliest.

whyNot.0: His daughter 'had already fallen asleep' by the time he finished, so finishing came later.
whyNot.1: He read the note last, after finishing his shift.
whyNot.3: Getting home follows the end of his shift, which came after the note was left.

explain.body: While, meanwhile, during and at the same time place events side by side. Neither comes before the other.

test.q:
Read the passage.

During the fire drill, staff closed every patient door. At the same time, the charge nurse counted patients on each hall. After the all-clear, staff reopened the doors.

Which event happened at the same time as closing the patient doors?
options: The all-clear was sounded
Staff reopened the doors
The nurse counted patients
The fire drill was scheduled
test.why: 'At the same time' links the patient count to the door closing during the drill.

whyNot.0: The all-clear came after the drill actions.
whyNot.1: Doors were reopened after the all-clear.
whyNot.3: Scheduling the drill is never mentioned.

explain.body: In a process, each step depends on the one before. Look for words like 'once', 'as soon as', 'after' and 'before', even when the steps are described out of order.

test.q:
Read the passage.

Once the bread dough has doubled in size, punch it down and shape it into a loaf. The dough rises after it is kneaded for 10 minutes. Bake the loaf only after it has risen a second time.

What is the correct order?
options: Knead, rise, shape, bake, rise again
Knead, rise, shape, rise again, bake
Rise, knead, shape, rise again, bake
Knead, shape, rise, rise again, bake
test.why: Knead first; the dough then rises; once doubled, it is punched down and shaped; it rises a second time; then it is baked.

whyNot.0: Baking comes only after the second rise.
whyNot.2: The dough rises after it is kneaded, not before.
whyNot.3: Shaping comes once the dough has doubled, so the first rise comes before shaping.
